sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的Dealbook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过nytimes.com进行部分采访的直播，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: November 18th.
If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, the American shooting miscalculations and misjudgments that led to the stunningly fast collapse of Afghanistan and to the scenes of chaos in Kabul.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来聊聊美国的误判和失策，这些错误导致了阿富汗惊人迅速的崩溃以及喀布尔的混乱局面。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, David Sanger.
sentences.zh: 我采访了我的同事大卫·桑格。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday,
sentences.zh: 今天是周二，

sentences.en: August 17th.
David, I want to start with the latest developments inside Kabul now that it has fallen into the hands of the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 大卫，我想先从喀布尔落入塔利班手中后的最新进展谈起。

sentences.en: Can you describe what that scene has been like over the past 24 hours or so?
sentences.zh: 你能描述一下过去24小时左右那里的场景吗？

sentences.en: Well, Michael, it was a weekend in which events unfolded, I think, much faster than anybody at the White House.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，这个周末发生的事情，我想比白宫里任何人的预想都要快得多。

sentences.en: Journalists, even people in Kabul thought they would.
sentences.zh: 记者们，甚至喀布尔当地的人都以为他们会撑得久一点。

sentences.en: If you're just joining us, we're getting new developments from Afghanistan, where the situation is changing there minute by minute.
sentences.zh: 如果你刚加入我们的节目，我们正在获取来自阿富汗的最新进展，那里的局势每分钟都在变化。

sentences.en: And by Sunday, the Taliban were at the gates of the city.
sentences.zh: 到了周日，塔利班已经兵临城下。

sentences.en: American Chinook helicopters have been spotted taking off and landing near the U.S.
sentences.zh: 有人看到美国的支奴干直升机在美国大使馆附近起降，

sentences.en: embassy as the Pentagon speeds troops into Kabul to get our people out.
sentences.zh: 因为五角大楼正在加紧向喀布尔派遣军队以撤离我们的人员。

sentences.en: We were seeing helicopters lifting off adjacent to the American embassy, clearly beginning to shuttle people out to the airport.
sentences.zh: 我们看到直升机在美国大使馆附近起飞，显然已经开始将人员运送到机场。

sentences.en: Richard said something at the top of his reporting, and I want to make sure that everybody heard it because it is significant.
sentences.zh: 理查德在报道开头提到了一件事，我想确保每个人都听到了，因为它非常重要。

sentences.en: The president,
sentences.zh: 总统，

sentences.en: President Ghani of Afghanistan, has left the country.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗总统加尼已经离开了该国。

sentences.en: By midday, President Ghani had fled the palace, was out of the country.
sentences.zh: 到中午时分，加尼总统已经逃离了总统府，离开了这个国家。

sentences.en: It looked like he had not even told his cabinet or his top aides.
sentences.zh: 看起来他甚至没有告诉他的内阁或高级助手。

sentences.en: You are looking at Taliban fighters inside the presidential palace.
sentences.zh: 你现在看到的是总统府内的塔利班武装人员。

sentences.en: By Sunday night, there were pictures of the Taliban showing up at the palace.
sentences.zh: 到了周日晚上，出现了塔利班出现在总统府的照片。

sentences.en: A stunning turnarounds of events.
sentences.zh: 局势发生了惊人的逆转。

sentences.en: And then on Monday, we saw these heartbreaking scenes from around the Hamid Karzai airport.
sentences.zh: 周一，我们看到了哈米德·卡尔扎伊国际机场周围令人心碎的场景。

sentences.en: There were thousands of Afghans trying to get through the gates, over the gates, anything they could do to get their families inside the airport compound in hopes of somehow flying
sentences.zh: 成千上万的阿富汗人试图穿过大门，翻过大门，想尽一切办法把家人带进机场大院，希望能以某种方式飞离

sentences.en: away from the Taliban's clutches.
sentences.zh: 塔利班的魔掌。

sentences.en: There was one moment where American Marines had to go open fire on some armed attackers who were coming in at the airfield.
sentences.zh: 有一次，美国海军陆战队不得不对一些冲向机场的武装袭击者开火。

sentences.en: There was another moment, perhaps the most devastating of all, where you saw people clinging to the landing gear of a plane as
sentences.zh: 还有另一个时刻，也许是最令人痛心的，你看到人们在飞机起飞时紧紧抓住起落架，

sentences.en: it was taking off, and some of them falling to their death.
sentences.zh: 随后一些人坠落身亡。

sentences.en: Well, David, I'm struck by just how many
sentences.zh: 大卫，我感到震惊的是，竟然有这么多

sentences.en: American officials, even the Secretary of State, for instance, who are expressing surprise at these developments, in some cases, shock.
sentences.zh: 美国官员，比如国务卿，他们对这些事态的发展表示惊讶，在某些情况下甚至是震惊。

sentences.en: And I want to talk through why this has all been such a surprise, and what misjudgments and miscalculations got us to this point where the Taliban could so quickly
sentences.zh: 我想探讨一下为什么这一切会如此令人意外，以及是什么样的误判和失策导致我们走到了这一步，让塔利班能够如此迅速地

sentences.en: seize control of the entire country before the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在美军完成撤离之前就夺取了整个国家的控制权。

sentences.en: even finished its military withdrawal.
sentences.zh: 我们该从哪里开始说起呢？

sentences.en: So where should we start?
sentences.zh: 我们该从哪里开始说起呢？

sentences.en: Well, I think the way you start, Michael, is to think about this decision in two different parts.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为迈克尔，开始讨论的方式是把这个决定分成两个部分来看。

sentences.en: So the first part was Biden's decision to get out.
sentences.zh: 第一部分是拜登撤军的决定。

sentences.en: He made a decision in April that he would have all American troops out of the country by September 11th.
sentences.zh: 他在四月份做出决定，要在9月11日之前让所有美军撤出该国。

sentences.en: And we could have a separate debate about whether that was a good decision or a bad decision, but you've heard his
sentences.zh: 我们可以就这是否是一个好决定进行单独的辩论，但你已经听过他的

sentences.en: fundamental argument, which was if we didn't manage to change the country in 20 years, staying another year or two years or five years was not going to make a material difference.
sentences.zh: 基本论点，即如果我们20年都没能改变这个国家，再待一年、两年或五年也不会有实质性的区别。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So at that moment, he basically started a clock.
sentences.zh: 所以在那一刻，他基本上启动了一个倒计时。

sentences.en: Once the clock started, it raised a whole second set of issues, which is how do you execute on this decision in a smooth way that hands over the power
sentences.zh: 一旦倒计时开始，就引发了一系列后续问题，即如何以平稳的方式执行这一决定，将权力移交给

sentences.en: to the Afghan government and doesn't give a huge opening to the Taliban?
sentences.zh: 阿富汗政府，同时又不给塔利班留下巨大的可乘之机？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think it's fair to say, Michael, that there are sort of four major assumptions.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，我认为可以公平地说，有四个主要的假设。

sentences.en: Some might say miscalculations that go into the execution of the American withdrawal and that some would argue contributed to the chaos that we've just seen.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能会说是误判，这些误判贯穿了美国撤军的执行过程，有人认为这导致了我们刚刚看到的混乱。

sentences.en: And David, what is the first of those assumptions slash miscalculations?
sentences.zh: 大卫，这些假设或误判中的第一个是什么？

sentences.en: Well, the first and the biggest assumption was that they had the luxury of time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，第一个也是最大的假设是他们拥有时间上的优势。

sentences.en: And the intelligence assessments that were on President Biden's desk suggested that they would probably have at least
sentences.zh: 放在拜登总统办公桌上的情报评估显示，他们可能至少还有

sentences.en: 18 months before Kabul could be seriously threatened by the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 18个月的时间，喀布尔才会受到塔利班的严重威胁。

sentences.en: And that over that time, the Afghan security forces would learn how to operate on their own so that they might actually be able to hold on to
sentences.zh: 而且在这段时间里，阿富汗安全部队将学会如何独立作战，这样他们或许真的能够守住

sentences.en: strategically vital parts of the country, especially the capital, Kabul.
sentences.zh: 国家战略要地，特别是首都喀布尔。

sentences.en: And that 20 years of training and equipping the Afghan security forces at a cost of at least $83 billion, and some would say much higher, had
sentences.zh: 而且20年来，耗资至少830亿美元（有人说更高）对阿富汗安全部队进行的训练和装备，已经

sentences.en: created an efficient force that had the capability to go deal with the Taliban and some big advantages.
sentences.zh: 打造出了一支高效的部队，有能力去对付塔利班，并拥有一些巨大的优势。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: The Afghan security forces had all of the hardware that we have been giving them and training them how to use and maintain.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗安全部队拥有我们一直提供给他们并训练他们使用和维护的所有硬件。

sentences.en: They had helicopters, they had aircraft.
sentences.zh: 他们有直升机，有飞机。

sentences.en: This was a huge advantage, obviously, in most battle situations.
sentences.zh: 显然，在大多数战斗情况下，这是一个巨大的优势。

sentences.en: And there were 300,000 Afghan security forces.
sentences.zh: 而且有30万阿富汗安全部队。

sentences.en: There were only 75,000 Taliban, by the best estimates.
sentences.zh: 据最好的估计，塔利班只有7.5万人。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So a major underpinning of the 18-month time horizon that turned out to be very flawed was this numerical
sentences.zh: 所以，那个被证明是非常错误的18个月时间跨度的主要支撑点，就是这个数字上的

sentences.en: disjunction between the Taliban, 75,000, and the Afghan security forces, 300,000.
sentences.zh: 巨大差异：塔利班7.5万人，而阿富汗安全部队有30万人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: On paper, the capabilities of the Afghans was tremendous.
sentences.zh: 从纸面上看，阿富汗人的能力是惊人的。

sentences.en: At one point, Biden said it was one of the best-equipped modern fighting forces in the world, some exaggeration.
sentences.zh: 拜登曾一度称其为世界上装备最精良的现代化作战部队之一，这有些夸张。

sentences.en: But on paper, it looked like the Afghan government had all the advantages.
sentences.zh: 但从纸面上看，阿富汗政府似乎占据了所有优势。

sentences.en: And that led to the second big assumption, which was that the Afghan forces had the same drive, the same determination to win that the Taliban did.
sentences.zh: 这导致了第二个大假设，即阿富汗部队拥有与塔利班相同的获胜动力和决心。

sentences.en: And why did the U.S.
sentences.zh: 为什么美国

sentences.en: get that so wrong?
sentences.zh: 会错得这么离谱？

sentences.en: How did we miscalculate the willingness, the eagerness, the determination of the Afghan military to defend their country against the Taliban?
sentences.zh: 我们是如何误判了阿富汗军队保卫国家对抗塔利班的意愿、渴望和决心的？

sentences.en: Well, you know, that's going to be, when the histories of this are written, I think, the biggest and toughest question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，当这段历史被写下来时，我认为这将是最大、最棘手的问题。

sentences.en: Because if you asked almost anybody who had fought alongside the
sentences.zh: 因为如果你问几乎任何与

sentences.en: Afghan units, they would tell you that at best, it was a mixed bag.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗部队并肩作战过的人，他们会告诉你，充其量也就是好坏参半。

sentences.en: They were extremely talented,
sentences.zh: 他们有极其出色、

sentences.en: extremely patriotic, extremely hardworking Afghan special forces.
sentences.zh: 极其爱国、极其刻苦的阿富汗特种部队。

sentences.en: And that there were moments in time, particularly around 2009, 2010, where those units fought right
sentences.zh: 而且在某些时刻，特别是在2009年、2010年左右，这些部队确实与美国

sentences.en: alongside the United States, learned a lot of lessons, and seemed to be a very effective fighting force.
sentences.zh: 并肩作战，学到了很多经验，看起来是一支非常有效的作战力量。

sentences.en: But I think the overwhelming sense that you get from people who spent a lot of time with
sentences.zh: 但我认为，从那些以士兵、承包商或其他身份在阿富汗待过很长时间的人那里得到的压倒性感觉是，

sentences.en: Afghanistan in some way, as soldiers or contractors or whatever, that they really weren't ready for it.
sentences.zh: 他们真的还没有准备好。

sentences.en: And so I think the big question is, did Joe Biden, a man who prides himself as the foreign policy
sentences.zh: 所以我认为最大的问题是，乔·拜登，一个以“外交政策总统”自居的人，

sentences.en: president, who was chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee during much of the Afghan war, how did he make a misjudgment that the Afghans were ready?
sentences.zh: 在阿富汗战争期间曾担任参议院外交关系委员会主席，他怎么会做出阿富汗人已经准备好了这种误判？

sentences.en: And that's a really pretty big mystery that we're all trying to grapple with today.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常大的谜团，我们今天都在努力去理解。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了吗？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《纽约时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So David, you had said that there were four assumptions and miscalculations that really help us understand how we got to this point in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 大卫，你刚才说有四个假设和误判，这确实有助于我们理解阿富汗局势为何发展到这一步。

sentences.en: What are the other two?
sentences.zh: 另外两个是什么？

sentences.en: Well, the third assumption, Michael, was that we had a well-planned system for evacuating the embassy
sentences.zh: 嗯，第三个假设，迈克尔，是我们有一个精心策划的撤离大使馆的系统，

sentences.en: and equally importantly, those 20,000, 25,000, maybe more Afghans and their families who had worked
sentences.zh: 同样重要的是，撤离那些为美国人工作、为非政府组织工作或为新闻机构工作，

sentences.en: for the Americans or worked for NGOs or worked for news organizations and needed to get out of the country if the Taliban were going to take over.
sentences.zh: 如果塔利班接管政权，他们就需要撤离该国的2万、2.5万甚至更多阿富汗人及其家属。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That seems like a basic obligation of a country that occupies another country for 20 years.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个占领另一个国家20年的国家的基本义务。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I mean, we knew from what the military did that you can get a lot of people out of Afghanistan in a big hurry because after all, the military was way ahead of schedule
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们从军方的行动中知道，你可以很快地把很多人从阿富汗撤出来，毕竟军方比计划提前了，

sentences.en: and got most of their combat troops out before the July 4th holiday.
sentences.zh: 在7月4日假期之前就撤出了大部分作战部队。

sentences.en: But it was a more complicated issue with these two different groups of civilians.
sentences.zh: 但这两类平民的问题更为复杂。

sentences.en: The State Department was hesitant to reduce the size of the embassy too quickly because they had a lot of diplomatic missions they needed to deal with the Afghan government.
sentences.zh: 国务院对过快缩减大使馆规模持犹豫态度，因为他们有许多需要与阿富汗政府处理的外交事务。

sentences.en: And then there were those interpreters and the helpers and those people who worked for news organizations like The Times.
sentences.zh: 还有那些翻译、助手以及为像《纽约时报》这样的新闻机构工作的人。

sentences.en: And that was difficult as well because the president of Afghanistan, Ashraf Ghani, had pressed President Biden during his meeting at the White
sentences.zh: 这也非常困难，因为阿富汗总统阿什拉夫·加尼在6月于白宫举行的会议上曾敦促拜登总统

sentences.en: House in June to keep a lot of these people in the country because he didn't want the image that the
sentences.zh: 让这些人留在国内，因为他不希望外界认为美国相信阿富汗政府会倒台。

sentences.en: United States believed that the Afghan government would fall.
sentences.zh: 问题是，当国家显然正在崩溃、塔利班占领更多领土时，你还能用飞机把这些人撤出来吗？

sentences.en: And the question was, as it became clear that the country was collapsing and the Taliban were taking more territory, could you get these people out of the country on aircraft?
sentences.zh: 而那个过程，文书工作，满足所有特殊移民身份的法定要求，这一切都慢得令人痛苦。

sentences.en: And that process, the paperwork, meeting all the statutory requirements for these special immigration status, that was all agonizingly slow.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Understood.
sentences.zh: 但是，考虑到这么多人的生命悬于一线，这些平民曾为美国和我们在阿富汗的军队冒过生命危险，为什么美国

sentences.en: But given the number of lives hanging in the balance, lives of civilians who had risked their lives for the United States and our military in Afghanistan, why didn't the U.S.
sentences.zh: 不采取措施加快这一进程，打破所有这些慢得令人痛苦的官僚主义，直接把事情办成呢？

sentences.en: take steps to expedite this process, to cut through all this agonizingly slow bureaucracy and just make this happen?
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题，迈克尔。

sentences.en: It's a great question, Michael.
sentences.zh: 我认为这将是未来几个月许多调查的主题。

sentences.en: And I think it's going to be the subject of a lot of investigations in coming months.
